common_name: Silver Stripe Philodendron (Heartleaf Philodendron with Silver-Striped Foliage)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Silver Stripe holds its variegation best with consistent bright indirect light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix. Silver Stripe is a heartleaf philodendron selection with each glossy, heart-shaped leaf marked by a distinct pale silvery-white central stripe running along the midrib, a simpler, more consistent variegation pattern than the irregular splashing found in some other variegated philodendron cultivars. Its trailing or climbing vine works equally well cascading from a hanging basket or trained up a moss pole, and it is a faster, more forgiving grower than many of the rarer variegated aroids in the trade. Let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings, and provide bright indirect light to keep the stripe pattern crisp, since low light causes new growth to green out.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Jose Buono is a compact, self-heading (non-climbing) selection that needs no moss pole or trellis.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix. Jose Buono produces large, broad, ruffled leaves in a bright lime-gold to chartreuse color that holds well with adequate light rather than fading to plain green, giving this self-heading philodendron a sunny, luminous presence distinct from the dark burgundy or plain green tones of many other compact philodendron hybrids. Its non-climbing, upright rosette habit needs no staking or support, making it a manageable tabletop or floor accent depending on pot size. Give it bright, indirect light for the best gold coloring, and keep it out of direct sun, which can scorch the pale foliage. Let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Albo Variegatum is frost-tender outside zones 10-11 and needs bright light to maintain its heavy white variegation.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix. Albo Variegatum carries irregular, unpredictable splashes and sectors of pure white scattered across each arrow-shaped green leaf, a bolder and more chlorophyll-poor variegation pattern than the softer center-shaded syngonium cultivars like White Butterfly, which means it grows more slowly and needs brighter light to stay vigorous. Young plants hold a compact, bushy, upright form and can later be trained onto a moss pole or trellis as they mature into a climbing habit. Pinch growing tips to keep the plant full, and watch for all-green reversion shoots, which grow faster than the variegated stems and should be pruned out to keep the plant from losing its variegation over time. As with other syngoniums, the sap can irritate skin and is toxic if chewed by pets.

common_name: Mint Monstera (Pale Mint-Green New Growth Swiss Cheese Plant)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container on a moss pole in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Mint needs strong indirect light to sustain its pale coloring.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container on a moss pole in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix. Mint is a Monstera deliciosa form whose new leaves emerge a pale, soft mint-green rather than the deep glossy green of the standard species, gradually deepening in color as each leaf matures and hardens off, giving an actively growing plant a two-toned look between fresh pale leaves and older darker ones. As leaves mature they develop the same iconic natural splits and holes as standard Monstera deliciosa once the plant is large enough. Provide a sturdy moss pole or trellis for the aerial roots to grip as it climbs, wipe dust from the large leaves periodically, and let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings.
